--- title: Query with DuckDB description: Query the public OmicIDX Parquet with DuckDB over anonymous HTTPS. Covers the published database, the SRAdb- and GEOmetadb-compatible tables, and the raw source tables. --- OmicIDX publishes every table as Parquet over anonymous HTTPS. [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org) reads only the parts of each file that a query needs, so you can query tens of millions of rows from a laptop without downloading anything first. The examples on this page ran against `latest/` when the page was built. Each SQL example has an **Open in DuckDB Shell** link that runs it in your browser, and the [playground](../playground.qmd) has an editable query box. ## What's published The base URL is: ``` https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/ ``` (The older `https://data.omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/` serves the same files.) Under it, `latest/` is rebuilt every night. Each night also gets an immutable `v{YYYY-MM-DD}/` folder, kept for 30 days. See [Versions and citation](versions-and-citation.qmd) for which to use, and [Releases](../releases.qmd) for what's there now. Each folder contains: | Path | What it is | |---|---| | `.parquet` | One file per source table: `sra_studies`, `sra_samples`, `sra_experiments`, `sra_runs`, `sra_accessions`, `geo_series`, `geo_samples`, `geo_platforms`, `geo_series_with_rnaseq_counts`, `biosamples`, `bioprojects`, `pubmed_articles` | | `sradb/
.parquet` | SRAdb-compatible tables | | `geometadb/
.parquet` | GEOmetadb-compatible tables | | `omicidx.duckdb` | A small DuckDB database with a view over every Parquet file | | `views.sql` | The same views as plain SQL | | `restore.sql` | Builds a local copy of every table (see [Work offline](#work-offline)). Older dated folders don't have it | | `manifest.json` | Publish date, transform commit, lake snapshot id, row counts | You can browse a folder listing in your browser, e.g. [`latest/`](https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/). ## Attach the database `omicidx.duckdb` is a few hundred KB of view definitions. Attach it over HTTPS and query the views. The data stays remote. ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} ATTACH 'https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/omicidx.duckdb' AS omicidx (READ_ONLY); USE omicidx; ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} SELECT run_accession, study_title FROM sradb.rnaseq_runs WHERE taxon_id = 9606 -- human LIMIT 10; ```
Table: Displaying records 1 - 10 |run_accession |study_title | |:-------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| |DRR391952 |Spatial transcriptome analysis of human oral cancers | |DRR391953 |Spatial transcriptome analysis of human oral cancers | |DRR391954 |Spatial transcriptome analysis of human oral cancers | |DRR391955 |Spatial transcriptome analysis of human oral cancers | |DRR391969 |Transcriptome analysis of human gingival epithelial cells treated with short-chain fatty acids | |DRR391970 |Transcriptome analysis of human gingival epithelial cells treated with short-chain fatty acids | |DRR391971 |Transcriptome analysis of human gingival epithelial cells treated with short-chain fatty acids | |DRR394097 |Single Cell RNA sequence of clinical breast cancer stem-like cells | |DRR394098 |Single Cell RNA sequence of clinical breast cancer stem-like cells | |DRR394099 |Single Cell RNA sequence of clinical breast cancer stem-like cells |
::: DuckDB loads its `httpfs` extension automatically for `https://` paths. If your install can't auto-load extensions, run `INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;` first. ## Read a Parquet file directly Every table is a plain file, so you can skip the database and use `read_parquet`: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} SELECT count(*) AS n FROM read_parquet('https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/biosamples.parquet'); ```
Table: 1 records | n| |--------:| | 60484224|
::: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} SELECT study_accession, title, study_type FROM 'https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/sra_studies.parquet' WHERE bioproject = 'PRJNA1147303'; ```
Table: 1 records |study_accession |title |study_type | |:---------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------| |SRP525855 |Platelets Transfer Aldolase via Extracellular Vesicles to Facilitate the Metabolic Reprogramming of Kupffer Cells in Acute Liver Injury |Transcriptome Analysis |
::: Filters and column selection are pushed down, so only the matching parts of a file are fetched. `pubmed_articles.parquet` is about 37 GB, so filter it in place. ## SRAdb-compatible tables (`sradb`) A modernized [SRAdb](https://bioconductor.org/packages/SRAdb/) schema. Legacy column names are kept where the data still exists, always-empty columns are dropped, and BioProject, GEO, and PubMed cross-references are added. | Table | One row per | |---|---| | `sradb.study` | SRA study (SRP/ERP/DRP) | | `sradb.sample` | SRA sample (SRS/ERS/DRS) | | `sradb.experiment` | SRA experiment (SRX/ERX/DRX) | | `sradb.run` | SRA run (SRR/ERR/DRR) | | `sradb.sra` | run, joined with its experiment, sample, and study | | `sradb.run_with_study` | run, with study title, type, and BioProject | | `sradb.rnaseq_runs`, `sradb.wgs_runs` | `run_with_study` filtered by library strategy | | `sradb.human_runs`, `sradb.mouse_runs` | `run_with_study` filtered by taxon | ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} SELECT study_accession, study_title, bioproject_accession, pubmed_ids FROM sradb.study WHERE study_accession = 'SRP000001'; ```
Table: 1 records |study_accession |study_title |bioproject_accession |pubmed_ids | |:---------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|:--------------------|:----------| |SRP000001 |Paired-end mapping reveals extensive structural variation in the human genome |PRJNA33627 |17901297 |
::: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} -- RNA-seq runs for one BioProject SELECT run_accession, platform, instrument_model, total_bases FROM sradb.run_with_study WHERE bioproject = 'PRJNA1147303' AND library_strategy = 'RNA-Seq'; ```

::: ## GEOmetadb-compatible tables (`geometadb`) A modernized [GEOmetadb](https://bioconductor.org/packages/GEOmetadb/) schema: series (`gse`), samples (`gsm`), platforms (`gpl`), the `gse_gsm` and `gse_gpl` link tables, and `geo_supplemental_files`. ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} -- Series with NCBI-computed RNA-seq counts SELECT gse, title FROM geometadb.gse WHERE has_geo_computed_rnaseq LIMIT 10; ```
Table: Displaying records 1 - 10 |gse |title | |:---------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| |GSE240902 |Single-nucleoid architecture reveals heterogeneous packaging of mitochondrial DNA [RNA-seq] | |GSE241020 |CD56-mediated activation of human natural killer cells is triggered by Aspergillus fumigatus galactosaminogalactan | |GSE241164 |Impact of bacterial derived microvesicles on gene expression of Caco2 cells. | |GSE241167 |Bacterial lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation promotes iron accumulation in human adipocytes | |GSE241430 |Longitudinal modeling of human neuronal aging reveals the contribution of the RCAN1-TFEB pathway to Huntington's disease neurodegeneration | |GSE241621 |Mutation-specific pathophysiological mechanisms of AFF3 differently influence transcriptome profiles | |GSE241649 |Pharmaceutical inhibition of RAS overcomes cytokine mediated resistance to FLT3 inhibition in FLT3-ITD+ AML [RNA-seq] | |GSE241702 |Mucosal CCL28 Chemokine Improves Protection against Genital Herpes through Mobilization of Antiviral Effector Memory CCR10+CD44+ CD62L-CD8+ T Cells and Memory CCR10+B220+CD27+ B Cells into the Infected Vaginal Mucosa | |GSE241796 |The helicase domain of human Dicer prevents RNAi-independent activation of antiviral and inflammatory pathways | |GSE241816 |Cytoglobin overexpression-dependent transcriptomic changes in A375 melanoma cells |
::: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} -- All samples in a series SELECT gsm FROM geometadb.gse_gsm WHERE gse = 'GSE118849'; ```
Table: Displaying records 1 - 10 |gsm | |:----------| |GSM3349112 | |GSM3349115 | |GSM3349119 | |GSM3349120 | |GSM3349118 | |GSM3349110 | |GSM3349113 | |GSM3349117 | |GSM3349109 | |GSM3349111 |
::: ## Source tables The source tables (`sra_runs`, `geo_samples`, `biosamples`, …) keep the upstream record shape, including nested lists of attributes and identifiers. In `omicidx.duckdb` they're views in the default schema, so after `USE omicidx` you can write `FROM sra_studies`. Older dated databases contain only the `sradb` and `geometadb` views; use `read_parquet` for source tables there. ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} -- Unnest SRA study attributes SELECT accession, a.tag, a.value FROM 'https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/sra_studies.parquet', unnest(attributes) AS t(a) LIMIT 10; ```
Table: Displaying records 1 - 10 |accession |tag |value | |:---------|:-----------------|:------------| |SRP687251 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA1106569 | |SRP692237 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA832731 | |SRP707907 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA489243 | |SRP655435 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA1223840 | |SRP363785 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA815648 | |SRP595562 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA1295909 | |SRP595664 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA81359 | |SRP584239 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA1261087 | |SRP651796 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA1090498 | |SRP569400 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA1120815 |
::: ## Work offline For heavy use, make a local copy. `restore.sql` copies every table of a folder into a local DuckDB file, with the same schemas and names as the views, then checks each table's row count against the folder's `manifest.json`: ```bash curl -O https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/restore.sql duckdb omicidx-local.duckdb < restore.sql duckdb -readonly omicidx-local.duckdb -c "SELECT count(*) FROM sradb.study" ``` A full copy is tens of GB, most of it `pubmed_articles` and `biosamples`. In R, [`omicidx_download()`](r-omicidxr.qmd#a-local-copy) does the same. To copy only a few tables, download their Parquet files and point DuckDB at them: ```bash curl -O https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/sradb/study.parquet duckdb -c "SELECT count(*) FROM 'study.parquet'" ``` ## Notes - Requests are anonymous HTTPS range requests. Behind a strict firewall, allow `omicidx.cancerdatasci.org`. - Any recent DuckDB release works. This page was built with DuckDB 1.5.6 (R package).
